items._cn_summary: 该文介绍的是1996年由德国地下厂牌abRECt发行的一张极为罕见的7寸黑胶唱片，限量100张手工编号，封面采用混凝土材质手工制作，配以多张附件卡片与说明书，体现出极端的物性美学与地下音乐制作理念。音乐风格归属于Noise与Experimental范畴，作品以电子噪音、田野环境声采样与手风琴、人声等非常规元素交织为主。两首曲目均超过七分钟，分别为夜幕低鸣（A面）与白昼低语（B面），形成明暗对照式的声响叙事。参与的两位音乐人Die Totgeburt与C.K.以合成器、采样器、效果器为核心工具，另一位Schüldis则提供声音素材，呈现出德语区工业噪音场景中典型的非旋律化、沉浸式的声学探索。然而原文仅为唱片信息罗列，缺乏实质性的乐评内容，无法深入评判其艺术价值与聆听体验。

items.body: Review by rdtprog — This is a live performance recorded in June 2017 where the band played the full "I Me Myself" andsongs from "The Way," "The Lamplighter," "Insomnia," and 3 unreleased tracks. The stage setup ismade in a special visual design with projections to illustrate the contrast between shadow andlight. This live release explores different styles of music, from symphonic, space, and ambient. Youcan hear in some epic songs the influence of the song "Echoes" from Pink Floyd. There is a cinematicatmosphere throughout the show, which was the band's intention. Don't expect high-definition picturequality, but the music is the main highlight here. It's been a few years since I have listened tothe band's albums, so I was a bit surprised by the eclectic nature of the music here but verypleased with the whole live show. He's just sad that the band doesn't make any more music andstopped touring during the covid virus.
items._genre: symphonic prog / space rock / ambient / cinematic
items._cn_summary: 这是ANIMA MUNDI乐队2017年6月的现场演出录像，收录了完整专辑《I Me Myself》以及《The Way》《The Lamplighter》《Insomnia》中的曲目和三首未发表作品。舞台设计以明暗对比的投影为视觉核心，音乐横跨交响、太空与氛围三种风格。部分史诗段落可听到Pink Floyd《Echoes》的影响，整体营造出贯穿始终的电影感氛围。录像画质并非高清水准，但音乐本身是真正值得关注的焦点。乐评人对乐队这种兼收并蓄的音乐特质感到惊喜，同时也遗憾乐队在疫情期间停止了创作与巡演。作为一张现场专辑，它更偏向对已有作品的演绎呈现，而非实验性突破，但在氛围营造和跨类型融合方面展现了乐队的综合音乐素养。

items.album: PABLO EL ENTERRADOR Pablo "El Enterrador" (Symphonic Prog, 1983)
items.excerpt: Review by Hrychu — 1983 wasn't the best year for organic sounding symphonic prog rocking in the so called "WesternWorld". items.body: Review by Hrychu — 1983 wasn't the best year for organic sounding symphonic prog rocking in the so called "WesternWorld". By the time Pablo: El Enterrador's sole opus came out, every 'big' prog player wanted tohave a streamlined arena pop sound to hit the radios and dance floors, and the only ones who weredoing the big overblown prog rock shtick, were from the poorer areas, like Eastern Europe, or inthis case South America, where the then-current radio trends were a few years behind. But I'm gladhistory went the way it did! Because this album is superb. The songs are really well written andperformed. The band did their thing while balancing between the the two following tropes: catchyhooks and the compositionally dense extended progressive rock bits. I personally believe that it'snot easy to maintain that balance and end up with falling to the pitfall of either having a popalbum with too much unfitting prog fusiony workouts or a prog album filled with simplified hook-driven padding. That's where Yes failed when they came out with Going For The One. That's whereGenesis failed, when they did And Then There Were Three, imo.Speaking of Genesis: the piano player Omar Lopez really went to impressively great lengths on howmuch that late 70's Tony Banks Yamaha CP80 tone could be emulated. It doesn't sound just like awannabe, at times I'm genuinely under the impression of Banks' rig being remotely channeled toArgentina. However, the Genesis similarities more or less end there and they aren't as obvious inother aspects of the sonic palette. Jose Maria Blanc's Rioplatese Spanish vocals are a totallydifferent beast to Phil Collins' mannerisms or even Kim Beacon's Elton John influenced vocal work onACF by Tony Banks. In contrast with Genesis' snappy, rhythmical and straight to the point pop/rockapproach and maybe just occasional jazz fusiony moments here and there, the songwriting and chordchange choices on Pablo: El Enterrador are much more on the mellow and soulful jazz fusion side,with frequent seventh/ninth chord ornaments and swinging solos. At times the sound reminds me moreof the keyboard-dominated Italian prog groups like Festa Mobile, Sensitiva Immagine or Locanda DelleFate than of Genesis.Unless you happen to own the original pressing of the LP on vinyl, in perfect condition, you're outof luck in terms of the sound quality. The master tapes were lost so all the reissues of the album,whether digital or vinyl were sourced from a really badly preserved LP copy, run through quitedestructive de-noising on top of that. Shame.
items._genre: symphonic prog / jazz fusion / progressive rock
items._cn_summary: 这张1983年阿根廷乐队的专辑在交响前卫摇滚的框架下融入了浓郁的爵士融合色彩。钢琴手Omar Lopez刻意模仿Tony Banks晚期Yamaha CP80的电钢琴音色，在和弦进行中大量使用七和弦、九和弦装饰，并配以摇摆感的独奏段落，使整体听感偏向柔顺的爵士融合一面，而非Genesis式的干脆流行摇滚路线。乐队在朗朗上口的旋律钩子与结构复杂的扩展段落之间取得了平衡，这一点被评论者拿来与Yes、Genesis后期的取舍失败作对比。人声采用阿根廷里奥普拉滕塞地区的西班牙语演唱，与英美主流前英语境形成距离。值得注意的是母带磁带已佚失，所有再版均源自保存极差的LP翻录再经降噪处理，音质受损严重，对于不在意的听众而言，仍可一窥这张融合了Genesis键盘美学与意大利前卫摇滚氛围、被埋没的南美佳作。

items.body: Review by VianaProghead — Review N� 974Porcupine Tree is an English progressive rock band that was formed in 1987 in Hemel Hempstead, Hertfordshire. This is undoubtedly Steven Wilson's most successful and projected musical project of all, as evidenced by the band's popularity. Porcupine Tree consists of a mixture of progressive rock, psychedelic rock, avant-garde experimentalism and heavy metal. It's defined by many fans of the progressive rock community and by the band's members themselves as an art rock music style. The official debut studio album of the band "On the Sunday of Life..." was released in 1992. Porcupine Tree initially remained a Wilson's one-man project. So, the line up on "On the Sunday of Life..." was only made of Steve with some other musicians as guests. The same happened with their second work "Up The Downstair".So, "Up The Downstair" is the second studio album of Porcupine Tree that was released in 1993. The line up on "Up The Downstair" is composed by Steven Wilson (vocals, guitar, bass guitar, keyboards and drum programming). "Up The Downstair" also has the participation of some other musicians. So we also have here the presence of Suzanne Barbieri (vocals), Richard Barbieri (electronics), Colin Edwin (bass guitar) and Gavin Harrison (drums), as guests.Although "Up The Downstair" was preceded by "On The Sunday Of Life...", Wilson sees "Up The Downstair" as Porcupine Tree's actual debut album by Porcupine Tree. After all, in the booklet of the most recent edition of this album he says that he cannot consider "On The Sunday Of Life?" as the real debut of the band, because that album consists of old previously recorded material from the period between 1988 and 1991. "Up The Downstair" contains ten songs on which Wilson tries to achieve a daring and well-thought-out synthesis between quite diverse music genres such as ambient, dance, electronic, krautrock, prog rock, psych rock and space rock. The album almost constantly moves back and forth between the youthful open-mindedness on the one hand and the mature ingenuity on the other. "Up The Downstair" incorporates some new components that are a herald of the more streamlined sound on their later works."What You Are Listening To..." is a short intro that fulfills the role of showing what to expect from the album and where someone presents what will be its music. Its synthesizers allow it to blend subtly with the next track. "Synesthesia" has a catchy beat, an exciting rhythm guitar and sensational solos performed by Wilson. This song comes with a somewhat simplistic rhythm, but the noticeable combination of pop and Floyd extractions, especially the beautiful Floydish guitar steered by the inclusion of electronic elements, makes up for it. "Monuments Burn Into Moments" with just 22-seconds, can be called as a kind of a "preparation track" for the next one. "Always Never" is a strong song with clear Pink Floyd reminiscences. This is a spacey and a fantasy song, with the acoustic guitars and climatic synths paving the way until heavy riffs invade the soundscapes in a sweeping explosion accompanied by prominent powerful drums. The title track is a 10-minute instrumental track that begins with ambient sounds. Then, an electronically generated choir intones a sombre melody that runs through the rest of this title. After a while, a rather simple rhythm sets in, but numerous electronic effects and a choir that keeps appearing give the piece an extremely dense, fascinating atmosphere. "Not Beautiful Anymore" reverts to the spoken verse at the beginning, until energizing drums open up a more exciting rock section, with the bass line and slightly distorted guitar riffs providing a great moment. "Siren" is a short ambient piece, a strange but concise intro to the next track, as happened with "Monuments Burn Into Moments". "Small Fish" has a Floyd atmosphere. It's not particularly complex, but the spherical keyboards, Gilmour's guitar work, Steven's melodic vocals and its spatial sound texture are draws and fascinate. "Burning Sky" is an instrumental that starts slower and spacey with synthesizers, but soon after offers a strong guitar and the splendid drums of Harrison. It works in repetition of chords, yet, in each movement of the musical segments the textures are enriched by the sound effects. "Fadeaway" ends the album with delicate keyboard sounds, gentle guitar and Wilson's almost whispered vocals. It has a sad, solemn beauty that stays with us after the album is finished, making it a great closing track with its space atmosphere.Conclusion: "Up The Downstair" shows Steve Wilson displaying all his inventive side and technical ability in a very consistent album. Perhaps the great virtue of this work is the ability to create an absolutely unique experience, based on sound atmospheres notably influenced by Pink Floyd and Ozric Tentacles, integrating different styles in smooth compositions and great combinations of ethereal and traveling keyboards, climatic drums and space guitars. The emphasis on an atmosphere built around an addictive and connected set of tracks, while still possessive of a somewhat immature sound, was a step forward in relation to "On The Sunday Of Life..." and certainly a step in the right direction. With "Up The Downstair" Porcupine Tree shows why they belong to the most important prog rock bands of the 90's.Prog is my Ferrari. Jem Godfrey (Frost*)

items._cn_summary: 这是英国乐队Porcupine Tree于1993年发行的第二张录音室专辑，由Steven Wilson主导创作，参与编曲的还有键盘手Richard Barbieri、贝斯手Colin Edwin及鼓手Gavin Harrison等。Wilson将本张专辑视为乐队真正的首作，因前一张作品主要由1988至1991年间积累的旧素材拼合而成。专辑横跨氛围、舞曲、电子、克拉夫特摇滚、前卫摇滚与迷幻太空摇滚等多种领域，在青涩大胆与成熟匠心之间反复摆渡，并预示了乐队后期更为精炼的声响走向。Wilson在音墙上营造出大量Pink Floyd式的回响与宇宙感，吉他独奏与电子音色相互渗透，曲目之间以简短的氛围片段串联过渡。整体呈现出从个人化项目向完整乐队形态过渡阶段的探索气质。

items.body: Review by A Crimson Mellotron — The third chapter in Rivers of Nihil's tetralogy of albums representing the four seasons is theambitious and sombre progressive death metal opus 'Where Owls Know My Name', which is the recorddepicting autumn. This is a relentless conceptual album that offers a relatively accessibletechnical sound replete with aggressive riffs, soothing saxophone solos, fabulous mellotroninterludes, and overall sophisticated arrangements. Furthermore, Rivers of Nihil combine beautifullyharsh vocals with clean ones, and often include atmospheric, keyboard-laden passages, which byitself echoes the poignant sound of retro prog. Ideally, this album reminisces the unthinkablemusical marriage between Camel and Meshuggah - emotive melodies, introspective lyrics andpsychedelic undertones are combined with an overt technicality and death metal dynamics.Now, such eclectic extreme metal albums often remain misunderstood, and I believe it is preciselybecause of the fusion of two disparate musical universes. Yet 'Owls' offers an elegant and evocativesound that bridges these two universes in a masterful way, even if the production style on thisalbum is rather old-school. Of the ten tracks appearing on this LP, there are two shorterinstrumentals that serve either as an introduction (the first track) and an interlude (track six),while all of the remaining eight songs feature vocalist Jake Dieffenbach who basically delivers acrushing performance all throughout. Some of the excellent compositions on this record include 'TheSilent Life', which is a song that combines the brutality of Rivers' riffs with their extravagantprog pedigree, and captures the first of several gorgeous saxophone solos. We then have 'A Home', asong that is slightly darker, with a dense and heavy writing, and the epic 'Subtle Change', which isan eight-minute-long track with a complex structure and some hauntingly moody parts, and remains oneof the band's most progressive-minded pieces. The instrumental 'Terrestria III: Wither' isinteresting interlude, once again playing with that ominous atmosphere that the album thriveswithin, while the final minutes feature no less excellent songs like 'Death Is Real' and the near-perfect title track. What I appreciate the most about 'Owls' is the incorporation of psychedelic,fusion, and prog elements as well as the moody metallic sound, which to me makes this one of Riversof Nihil's most remarkable releases to date.

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是河流众神乐队四季四部曲的第三作，以秋天为主题，技术性前卫死亡金属为基底，融入大量前卫摇滚元素。专辑将侵略性的金属失真riff与萨克斯独奏、键盘氛围段落、mellotron间奏并置，试图在Meshuggah式的极端动态与Camel式情感旋律之间架桥。Jake Dieffenbach的人声在嘶吼与清声之间切换，十首曲目中有两首器乐短曲作为引子与过渡，其余作品结构复杂，氛围阴郁。制作走复古路线，混音偏老派。整体而言，这是一次跨风格嫁接的尝试，将死亡金属的重量与前卫摇滚的内省气质结合，萨克管的加入为极端金属提供了少见的柔情维度，但在融合深度与原创性上仍受限于类型框架。

items.body: Review by UMUR — "Still Life" is a double album live release by US progressive metal act Fates Warning. The album wasreleased through Massacre Records in October 1998. It bridges the gap between Fates Warning�s eighthand ninth full-length studio albums "A Pleasant Shade of Gray" (1997) and "Disconnected" (2000).Disc 1 features a live performance of the full "A Pleasant Shade of Gray" album while disc 2features six tracks from the band�s four 1988-1994 albums and "Prelude to Ruin" from "Awaken theGuardian" (1986). So, basically songs from all Ray Alder fronted Fates Warning albums (up untilthen) and one track from a John Arch fronted Fates Warning album.As if a full performance of the 51:56 minutes long concept album "A Pleasant Shade of Gray"including all sub-tracks wasn�t enough, Fates Warning have also opted to include a live performanceof their second longest epic, the nearly 21 minutes long "The Ivory Gate Of Dreams", so it�s safe tosay Fates Warning are firing on all cylinders on "Still Life". As for the remaining tracks it�salways hard to satisfy every fan when you are eight albums into your career and that career isdivided into two chapters with two different vocalists, but I�d say that tracks like "The EleventhHour", "Monument", and "Point Of View" belong here just fine and the nod towards the Arch-frontedera of Fates Warning with "Prelude to Ruin" is a nice touch too, although hearing Ray Alder sing thesong takes some getting used to. He does a great job though and provides the song with his ownidentity.Fates Warning was down to a trio at this point (Lead vocalist Ray Alder, Drummer Mark Zonder, andguitarist Jim Matheos), but on "Still Life" they are assisted by three session musicians and themusical performances are on a high level throughout. Bassist Joey Vera (who would soon become apermanent member of Fates Warning) sings harmony vocals, which is an important detail as a lot ofFates Warning�s songs feature harmony vocals and choirs. The audience helps the best they can toothough. The best example of that is probably when they sing the beautiful and epic wordless part on"The Eleventh Hour". I�m getting goosebumps because it feels like being there in that venue withthem. There�s some great audience participation all the way through "Still Life" and it�s a livealbum which actually feels like it was recorded live without too many overdubs despite featuring anexcellent live production job. "Still Life" is upon conclusion a high quality live album from FatesWarning and a 4 star (80%) rating is deserved.(Originally posted on Metal Music Archives).
items._cn_summary: 这张1998年发行的双碟现场专辑收录了Fates Warning完整演绎概念专辑《A Pleasant Shade of Gray》的全部曲目，加上从1986至1994年间多张录音室专辑中精选的六首作品。乐队当时精简为三人核心阵容——主唱Ray Alder、鼓手Mark Zonder与吉他手Jim Matheos，并邀请三位客座乐手补全编制，其中Bassist Joey Vera负责和声部分，对乐队复杂的多声部合唱结构至关重要。录音采用高质量现场制作，保留了观众的合唱互动，特别是《The Eleventh Hour》中的无词段落营造出强烈的现场临场感。整张专辑横跨乐队Ray Alder主唱时期的全部作品，并向John Arch时期致敬，加入《Prelude to Ruin》一曲。乐评给予四星（80%）评价，肯定其在编曲完整性、演奏水准与现场氛围还原度方面的表现。

items.body: Jacqui Hunt “Desiderium” is the new album from Australian vocalist Jacqui Hunt, of Single Gun Theory, released on June 26, 2026 through QUSP. The 11-track “Desiderium” is her first solo album in 18 years, issued on CD, limited-edition vinyl and digital. Jacqui Hunt brings an ethereal, electronic sound that mixes cinematic synths with piano and organic instrumentation. She describes the album as “like stepping out of your body for a while and grounding back to earth — floating on a synth wave while holding the raw reality of a simple piano. The bones that connect to the human voice like a string of air as it floats to the ether and returns to base.” Inside Jacqui Hunt ‘Desiderium’ “Desiderium” runs 11 tracks: “Desiderium,” “Look At The Sky,” “Planet,” “Cecilia,” “Cape Of Light,” “This Love,” “Temple Of Illumination,” “Follow Me Here,” “Cycles,” “Mother” and “Alice Magic.” Hunt recorded the album at QUSP Studios in Sydney, handling vocals, keys and production. Brian Conolly added synth, bass and guitar and engineered the record, Laurence Pike played drums, and Daniel Denholm contributed zither, strings and cello and mixed the album. Michael Lynch mastered it. The closing track also appears as “Alice Magic (K.I.M. Remix),” reworked by Kim Moyes of The Presets. The album is out on CD, limited-edition vinyl and digital. Hunt released an official video for “Planet”: About Jacqui Hunt Jacqui Hunt is an Australian vocalist who co-founded the electronic group Single Gun Theory in Sydney in 1986 with Kath Power and Pete Rivett-Carnac. The band released “Exorcise This Wasteland” in 1987, “Millions, Like Stars in My Hands, The Daggers in My Heart Wage War” in 1991 and “Flow, River of My Soul” in 1994, and was discovered for the Canadian label Nettwerk by Tom Ellard of Severed Heads. Hunt also sang on Delerium‘s album “Karma” (1997), the project of Bill Leeb and Rhys Fulber, contributing to the track “Euphoria (Firefly).” Her debut solo album, “Auraphonic,” appeared in 2008. “Desiderium,” released on June 26, 2026, is her first solo album since, and arrives 40 years after she co-founded Single Gun Theory.
items._genre: ethereal electronic / ambient / cinematic synth / art pop
items._cn_summary: 澳大利亚歌手Jacqui Hunt时隔18年发行个人专辑《Desiderium》，由QUSP厂牌发行，收录11首曲目。Hunt本人包揽人声、键盘与制作，搭档Brian Conolly负责合成器、贝斯与吉他，Laurence Pike演奏鼓，Daniel Denholm贡献齐特琴、弦乐与大提琴并完成混音。专辑将空灵人声与电影感合成器结合，辅以钢琴及原声乐器，Hunt将其描述为在半空中漂浮后回归大地的体验。终曲另附The Presets成员Kim Moyes的混音版本。Hunt早年与Single Gun Theory活跃于实验电子领域，1997年曾参与Delerium专辑录制，此次新作延续了她在氛围与电子之间游走的创作路线。

items.body: Real Farmer “Live at The Dalby Cafe” is a new four-track live EP from the Dutch band Real Farmer, released on June 26, 2026 through Strap Originals. The “Live at The Dalby Cafe” EP and a full performance video were captured at the Dalby Cafe in Margate, the first in a series of Strap Originals curated sessions. Real Farmer bring a post-punk-adjacent sound that mixes DIY punk, angular art-rock and noise. Real Farmer ‘Live at The Dalby Cafe’: the live EP “Live at The Dalby Cafe” holds four tracks: “Heart Out,” “Missing Link,” “The Pressure Of Others” and “Once More.” According to the band, the session was recorded in a single continuous take at the Dalby Cafe in Margate, filmed by Roger Sargent with audio by Jason Stafford. The EP follows the band’s second album, “Two Wrongs Don’t Make A Right,” released on May 1, 2026 through Strap Originals. Real Farmer shared the full performance video: Real Farmer 2026 tour dates According to Strap Originals, Real Farmer will support The Sisters of Mercy on the September dates in Spain, part of a run of European shows across the rest of the year. The Sisters of Mercy recently cancelled a festival to record a new album. July 11, 2026 — Pegnitz, Germany — Waldstock July 18, 2026 — Nijmegen, Netherlands — Valkhof Festival August 22, 2026 — Bioul, Belgium — La Carrière Festival August 28, 2026 — Groningen, Netherlands — Vera August 29, 2026 — Gent, Belgium — Free Openair 9030 September 23, 2026 — Bilbao, Spain — Santana 27 (with The Sisters of Mercy) September 24, 2026 — Madrid, Spain — Wagon (with The Sisters of Mercy) September 26, 2026 — Granada, Spain — La Industrial Copera (with The Sisters of Mercy) September 27, 2026 — Valencia, Spain — Roig Arena (with The Sisters of Mercy) September 29, 2026 — Barcelona, Spain — Paral·lel 62 (with The Sisters of Mercy) October 1, 2026 — Marseille, France — Cepac Silo October 2, 2026 — Nancy, France — L’Autre Canal October 4, 2026 — Frankfurt, Germany — Batschkapp November 8, 2026 — Esch-sur-Alzette, Luxembourg — Rockhal November 10, 2026 — Utrecht, Netherlands — TivoliVredenburg Ronda November 12, 2026 — Malmö, Sweden — Plan B November 13, 2026 — Gothenburg, Sweden — Trädgår’n November 15, 2026 — Oslo, Norway — Rockefeller November 16, 2026 — Stockholm, Sweden — Fållan About Real Farmer Real Farmer is a four-piece from Groningen, Netherlands, made up of Jeroen Klootsema (vocals), Marrit Meinema (bass, vocals), Leon Harms (drums) and Peter van der Ploeg (guitar, backing vocals). The band released its debut EP through Subroutine Records in 2019 and signed to Strap Originals, the label run by Pete Doherty, in 2023. The debut album “Compare What’s There” appeared in 2024, followed by the EP “RF II” in 2025 and the second album “Two Wrongs Don’t Make A Right” on May 1, 2026. “Live at The Dalby Cafe,” released on June 26, 2026, is the band’s first live EP and opens a new series of Strap Originals sessions.

items._cn_summary: 荷兰乐队Real Farmer于2026年6月发布四轨现场EP《Live at The Dalby Cafe》，在Margate的Dalby Cafe以单次连续录制完成，由Roger Sargent拍摄、Jason Stafford负责音频。作品延续其第二张专辑《Two Wrongs Don't Make A Right》的方向，将后朋克的冷峻骨架与DIY朋克、棱角分明的艺术摇滚以及噪音肌理相互叠加，乐器编制保持四人乐队的克制密度，依靠吉他切角与节奏组的张力推进情绪。乐队所属的Strap Originals厂牌由Pete Doherty运营，本次现场录制属于厂牌策划的首个策划系列现场之一。此外，乐队公布了2026年下半年密集的欧洲巡演日程，包括九月为The Sisters of Mercy西班牙场次做暖场，跨越德、比、法、瑞、挪等多国演出场地。

The Medea Project ‘Komēn: Facets’: two takes on a Kharon track Both tracks on the single rework “Purgatory: Trapped” from the 2025 album “Kharon.” The opener, “Purgatory Release,” was reimagined and remixed by Lucifer X of St. Lucifer, while “In Purgatory: Trapped” returns to an earlier incarnation of the song from the “Kharon” demos. The Medea Project shared a video alongside the single: The release lands as the band prepares to play the Darker Days festival at The International in Leicester on June 27, 2026, a gothic weekender whose lineup includes The March Violets, Guillotine Dream and Salvation. About The Medea Project The Medea Project is led by Brett Minnie, who carried the project from South Africa’s east coast to the United Kingdom, where it is now based in Nottingham. Minnie rebuilt the band in England and began playing shows in 2017, recording a self-titled debut EP that year. The project became a duo with the addition of drummer and percussionist Pauline Silver. The debut album “Sisyphus” arrived in 2020, followed by the EP “Reflections” in 2023 through Trepanation Recordings. The second album, “Kharon,” was released on June 20, 2025. In April 2026 the band issued the EP “Akkadian Artefacts,” a set of remixes by St. Lucifer’s Lucifer X, through BDB Productions. “Komēn: Facets,” released on June 26, 2026, continues that run and pulls the project further toward its dark ambient and electronica side.
items._cn_summary: The Medea Project 发布的双轨单曲收录了2025年专辑《Kharon》中作品的两种不同演绎版本。开场曲《Purgatory Release》由 St. Lucifer 的 Lucifer X 进行重混与再创作，呈现出电子化、俱乐部化的面貌；第二首《In Purgatory: Trapped》则回归了专辑原始 demo 阶段更早的版本。两首作品都建立在脉冲式合成器与暗黑氛围节奏之上，融合暗潮、doom 与电子元素。乐队主创 Brett Minnie 从南非迁至英国诺丁翰后逐步发展此项目，与鼓手 Pauline Silver 组成固定二人编制，发行轨迹从小厂牌自出版延伸至 Trepanation Recordings 及 BDB Productions。该单曲是其暗潮电子方向探索的延续，与即将到来的 Leicester 暗黑音乐节演出形成呼应。

items.body:
Since everyone else has written something about the centennials of Miles Davis and John Coltrane, why not join the parade? It is a good opportunity to look at the timeline of bassists the legendary trumpeter and saxophonist used. Born just under four months apart, the pair worked together under the elder Davis’ name periodically between Fall 1955 and Spring 1957 before a more steady affiliation in 1958-1960.

It is in that latter period that this analysis will begin, as it gives a convenient bit of serendipity: the fact that two of the their most famed albums were made in that period, Davis’ Kind Blue (March 2nd and April 22nd, 1959 for Columbia) and Coltrane’s Giant Steps (May 4th–5th and December 2nd, 1959). And the analysis will end with Coltrane’s death in 1967, which came during the tenure of Davis’ “second great quintet” and before his groups swelled and electrified during his fusion period.

As such, we begin with the same man, the bassist on both those albums: Paul Chambers. He had taken up the bass a decade earlier in his adopted home of Detroit (where he was a student at the seminal Cass Technical High School ... more on that later). He arrived in New York in 1954 at 19. By the time of Kind of Blue and Giant Steps, he had been on over 100 sessions from dozens of leaders, with multiple dates under Davis (with whom he had started working in late 1955) and Coltrane (who had used him for several albums in 1957-58 as well as both fellow sideman for many others and Chambers also hiring Coltrane for his own sessions). In addition to the five albums he led, Chambers played on sessions for Benny Golson, Curtis Fuller, J.J. Johnson, Lee Morgan, Red Garland, Sonny Clark, and Sonny Rollins.

The collaboration between Davis and Chambers was remarkably fruitful before and after Kind of Blue and solidified a part of Davis’ music that had previously seen widely differing players like Tommy Potter, Oscar Pettiford, Al McKibbon, and Percy Heath. The rest of 1959 saw multiple engagements around the country and closed with recordings that would be part of another monumental record, Sketches of Spain, that paired Davis’ group with the Gil Evans Orchestra. 1960 continued that momentum with more Sketches of Spain recording and almost non-stop touring, including two stretches in Europe, from Spring onward. 1961 and 1962 had more of the same activity, the documents being Someday My Prince Will Come and Quiet Nights. Then, quite suddenly, Chambers left Davis’ group in early February 1963.

It should be stated that Chambers did not restrict his activities solely to Davis, recording over four dozen albums during the period with, among many others, Jackie McLean, Wynton Kelly, Benny Golson, Hank Mobley, and Curtis Fuller. And after leaving Davis, he worked steadily with an array of leaders through the end of 1968, sadly passing away from tuberculosis caused and/or aggravated by drug abuse at only 33.

Stepping right into the Davis group was another Cass Technical High School alumnus: Ron Carter. Nearly 26, Carter was already prophesying his prolific career, participating in over three dozen albums since 1960, with the likes of Charli Persip, Yusef Lateef, Eric Dolphy, Don Ellis, Coleman Hawkins, Cecil Payne, Jaki Byard, Wes Montgomery, Bobby Timmons, Tadd Dameron, Dizzy Reece, Ken McIntyre, Milt Jackson, Benny Golson and others, plus waxing his leader debut, Where?, for Prestige subsidiary New Jazz in 1961.

It was Carter’s arrival that heralded Davis’ soon-to-be seminal band, though it took until Fall 1964 for its personnel to solidify. With Carter, Davis recorded Seven Steps To Heaven and played the Antibes festival in 1963. What is interesting though is while the “second great quintet” is thought of as a monolith, the bass chair had some upheaval/fluidity, depending on how you look at it. Gary Peacock – already a veteran and likely the only person to work for both Bud Shank and Albert Ayler – took the chair for nearly six weeks in the spring of 1964, Carter returning thereafter through the end of the year. 1965 began auspiciously with the January recording of E.S.P. but then things derailed with a convalescing Davis unable to play. And when he could, in November and December, Carter, a hot commodity, was absent, spelled by Peacock once more, then Reggie Workman, who had come up around the same time as Carter and had already come and gone in the groups of Coltrane. In 1966, Carter would return to the group but only partially, participating in East Coast performances, shows elsewhere having either Richard Davis, Carter’s only real equal in terms of fecundity, or in the Peacock mold of eclecticism, Eddie Gomez, returning permanently in October, just before the album Miles Smiles. 1967 was similar: Carter was on board when not busy elsewhere, Gomez on call, then Albert Stinson for one show (a little over two years before his passing – see Bass Tragedies column in Issue 94) and then another veteran, Buster Williams, for a tour (and playing on one track of the 1981-released compilation album Directions). Carter would fill a fixed point for all of 1967, including the albums Sorcerer and Nefertiti and would continue with Davis through the middle of 1968.

Like Chambers or perhaps even more so, Carter was also on the greater jazz scene during his tenure with Davis. He recorded on sessions led by his fellow Davis bandmates but also by everyone from Bobby Timmons, Charles Lloyd, Donald Byrd and Bobby Hutcherson to Jimmy Smith, Shirley Scott, Eddie Harris, and Stanley Turrentine, to name only a handful. He has, of course, gone on to be likely the most recorded bassist in jazz history.

Paul Chambers’ time under Coltrane was shorter and more intermittent. After Giant Steps he was part of, along with the rest of Davis’ period band, November 1959 recordings that would partly comprise Coltrane Jazz and be brought back 18 months later as one of three individual bassists taking part in the Africa/Brass recordings (though his contribution was only heard on the 1995 complete sessions version).

Also in 1959 was a Birdland engagement for Coltrane where either Ahmed Abdul-Malik or George Tucker, both established and close in age to Coltrane, were on bass.

In 1960 Coltrane hired the slightly younger Steve Davis in what seems to be his first professional engagement. Davis stayed in the band through the end of the year for all its live dates and played on music recorded in October and released piecemeal on My Favorite Things, Coltrane Jazz, Coltrane Plays the Blues, and Coltrane’s Sound. Though Davis lived until 1987, his credits after Coltrane were slight: the Mangione Brothers, Dave Burns, McCoy Tyner, Kenny Dorham, James Moody, Freddie McCoy, and Eddie Jefferson, all made in the ‘60s. One deviation in the year came via Coltrane’s shared date with Don Cherry, The Avant-Garde, where bass was handled by either Charlie Haden or Percy Heath.

1961 was a year in flux, bassist-wise, for Coltrane. He introduced a concept to which he would return later in the decade by using two bassists for an engagement at Chicago’s Sutherland Lounge in March: Raphael Don Garrett and Workman, the former, about six years younger, working with Roland Kirk, Paul Serrano, and Eddie Harris, the latter 11 years younger, sideman for Gigi Gryce, Donald Byrd, Duke Jordan, Richard Williams, and Dave Pike.

Workman would be part of the aforementioned Africa/Brass, as would, separately, another bassist, Art Davis, already with credits under Max Roach, Lee Morgan, Booker Little, Hal Mooney, Ernestine Anderson, Dizzy Gillespie, Leo Wright, Clifford Jordan/Sonny Red, Abbey Lincoln, and Booker Little. But in May they were together for Ole Coltrane and nearly a month at the Village Vanguard in August. Workman would become the fixed bassist for Coltrane through the end of the year for concerts, including a European tour, and a small portion of the Ballads album from the end of the year. An exception was Workman either alternating or alongside Jimmy Garrison for a November stint at the Village Vanguard.

If not for a family health crisis forcing Workman to leave the group at the end of 1961 and return to his native Philadelphia, he likely would have stayed with the band and jazz history been quite different. It should be said that Workman hardly is a footnote, becoming one of the most revered players of his generation. But it was Garrison who became the anchor. Born between Garrett and Workman, prior to joining Coltrane he had worked with Philly Joe Jones, Curtis Fuller, Kenny Dorham, Jackie McLean, JR Montrose, Walter Bishop, Jr., Ornette Coleman, Bill Barron, and Ted Curson.

Unlike Carter and Davis, once Garrison was on board, he stayed there. That was mostly to do with Coltrane’s packed schedule of touring and albums and that, unlike Davis, he was healthy and non-combustible. From 1962-1964, Garrison was omnipresent, including the bulk of Ballads, Duke Ellington & John Coltrane (where he split duties with Ellington’s period bassist Aaron Bell), 2018 discovery Both Directions At Once, John Coltrane And Johnny Hartman, Impressions, Crescent, another new millennium unearthed gem in Blue World, and closing out the year with Coltrane’s magnum opus A Love Supreme (which added Art Davis for a second day of recording, released as a second disc to the album’s deluxe edition in 2002).

In 1965 Garrison was still the main man but occasionally Davis would be alongside him: partially on The John Coltrane Quartet Plays in February and fully for June’s Ascension. Otherwise, Garrison was the sole bassist for performances and most of the other albums: Transition, Sun Ship, and Meditations. The exceptions without Davis were overdubs of Haden for the posthumously released Infinity and Garrett returning to play both bass and clarinet for Live In Seattle (as well as the 2021 archival release A Love Supreme: Live In Seattle), Om, and part of Kulu Se Mama.

1966 was even more Garrison-centric, with the only documented work including a second bassist shows in November and December with Lionel “Sonny” Johnson, the brother of Dewey Johnson, who had played on Ascension. The last year of Coltrane’s life, Garrison was there as well, with one notable absence: the Coltrane/Rashied Ali duet Interstellar Space.

Unlike Chambers or Carter, Garrison was kept so busy during his time with Coltrane that his outside discography at the time is meager, though it does include his sole leader date, Illumination! with the Elvin Jones/Jimmy Garrison Sextet. Otherwise it was sessions with Lorez Alexandria, Coltrane bandmate McCoy Tyner, Sonny Rollins, Bill Dixon, and Robert F. Pozar.

After Coltrane’s death, Garrison kept working but his documentation slowed, his two Blue Note dates with the Jones trio rounded out by Joe Farrell being the most enduring. There were also dates with Rolf and Joachim Kuhn, Clifford Thornton and Nathan Davis, and regular work with Alice Coltrane and Archie Shepp. His final recording came in early 1975 with Beaver Harris and Dave Burrell’s 360 Degree Music Experience. Garrison died of lung cancer in 1976 at 42.
items._cn_summary: 这篇乐评聚焦于Miles Davis与John Coltrane两位爵士巨匠合作时期所使用过的贝斯手谱系，从1958至1967年间的录音与演出线索展开。以Paul Chambers为起点，详述其在Kind of Blue与Giant Steps两张经典专辑中的核心地位，以及离开Davis组合后的广泛录音活动。文章更偏向音乐史考据风格，分析贝斯手在不同编制中的角色流转与人事更替，涵盖与Jackie McLean、Wynton Kelly等多位乐手的合作轨迹。整体属于学术性爵士乐评范畴，涉及编年史梳理与演奏家生涯回顾，但缺乏对音乐本身的听觉分析或声响层面的深度评论。

items.body: Review by kenethlevine — The subtle "I" at the end of the name here suggests that this second album might be the first in a line of "May" themed opuses by these relative newcomers. While in structure and overall effect similar to their 2024 full length debut, they are sounding more British isles and less scattershot Euro than before. Not to say this is any more original, what with JETHRO TULL comparisons likely to plague them forever, even though their commitment to being a Celtic rock band first and foremost is far more convincing than Ian Anderson's preference for diversification. This places them closer top the likes of a more patriarchal STEELEYE SPAN or even RUNRIG or OYSTERBAND territory. They do sing one track in Welsh which, combined with the GPS references of "Lakesongs of Elbid", belies possible ethnic origins. Perhaps not as prog or as wide ranging, it's also more consistent, hence making that final character in the title a welcome hint of the springboarding future.

items.body: Review by kev rowland — Protos was formed in 1977 by Rory Ridley-Duff (keyboards) and Steve Anscombe (guitars), and their 1982 debut album, 'One Day a New Horizon', had an expanded line-up which included Neil Goldsmith, Iain Carnegie and Nigel Rippon. By 1984 the band was no more, but Ridley-Duff and Anscombe stayed active in the music scene, and following on from a CD reissue of the album in 2006 they released a new album the following year. What we have here is a new keyboards and drums version of the original with Ridley-Duff being joined by drummer Alex Warwick. Apparently Anscombe was involved in the arrangements but was too ill to be musically active as he was suffering from a terminal illness, and on the front cover it states, "In memory of Stephen Anscombe".It is somewhat unusual for a band to revisit their debut so long after the original was released, and although I probably know more underground prog than many, I must confess I have never come across the original. This album has the same six songs but not knowing the debut I cannot comment on just how different it is. What did surprise me however is just how much I kept thinking of Soniq Theater while I was playing this, and I was somewhat surprised to see it wasn't Alfred when I looked to see what the album was. However, the use of "real" drums makes a significant difference and definitely adds to the polish on this release. It is not surprising to discover this is a remake of a much older album as it still has plenty of Eighties' feel about it, probably aided by the keyboard sounds being utilised. It is an interesting release as opposed to essential, and in some ways appears to have been influenced by Steve Hackett and Anthony Phillips' pastoral works, which is something of a weird thing to say given they are both guitarists and this is keyboards, but my mind works in weird and wonderful ways. It is a pleasant enough progressive romp, and I am sure anyone who has enjoyed the original release will want to seek this out.
items._cn_summary: Protos 乐队 1977 年成立，1982 年发布首张专辑，2024 年由创始人 Rory Ridley-Duff 与鼓手 Alex Warwick 重新录制键盘与鼓版本的旧作，以纪念已故吉他手 Steve Anscombe。整张专辑保留了原版六首曲目，但用真实鼓组替换了原版鼓机音色，键盘编曲主导全局，散发着浓厚的八十年代合成器质感。乐评人指出作品具有牧场派般的宁静氛围，隐约带有 Steve Hackett 与 Anthony Phillips 吉他的田园诗意色彩，但整体仍属传统的新前卫摇滚范畴，缺乏实验性突破与跨类型融合，定位为对原作感兴趣的乐迷的补充收藏，而非必听之作。

items.body: Calva Y Nada, the German electro and dark-wave project of Constantin Warter, release the live album “El calor de Zwickau” on October 2, 2026 through emmobiz Records. The label issues the Club Seilerstraße, Zwickau recording across vinyl and CD editions. Calva Y Nada bring a German electro and dark wave that mixes EBM rhythms and minimal-electronic textures with German- and Spanish-language vocals. The “El calor de Zwickau” set runs fifteen tracks, among them “Die Reise,” “Aufprall,” “Schmerzenskrone,” “Dias Felices,” “Habemus Papam,” “Fernes Leid,” “La pura mierda” and “Der Sturm,” closing with an encore of “Borriquito,” “Paradies” and “Rascheln.” Calva Y Nada ‘El calor de Zwickau’ editions emmobiz Records releases “El calor de Zwickau” on October 2, 2026 in several editions, including a double LP, an LP set, an LP box, a CD set, a CD box and a three-CD edition. Part of the run includes a bonus 7-inch or 3-inch CD with a one-off joint performance of “Deutschland” by Prager Handgriff and Calva Y Nada. The three-CD edition pairs the new “El calor de Zwickau” recording with the earlier “Live @ Club Seilerstraße” set and an encore disc. Side-Line covered the project’s 2024 “Live @ Club Seilerstraße Zwickau” release and the 2026 “La Pura Mierda” EP. About Calva Y Nada Calva Y Nada is the German electro and dark-wave project founded in 1990 by Constantin Warter, who records under the name Breñal. The project grew out of his earlier group Glatze des Willens — “Calva” is Spanish for the German word “Glatze” (bald). Calva Y Nada released early albums on Hyperium, including “Dias Felizes” (1991) and “Monologe eines Baumes” (1993), followed by “¡Palpita, Corazón, Palpita!” (1994) and a final studio album, “Schlaf,” in 1998. The project went quiet at the end of the 1990s and returned in the 2010s and 2020s. Since 2024, emmobiz Records has run a vinyl reissue and live program for the catalogue, and the 2026 EP “La Pura Mierda” marked its first new studio material since 1998. “El calor de Zwickau” continues that run with a live document released on October 2, 2026.

items.body: Black Sherif strips “Find A Way” back to an acoustic guitar loop in a minor key, a low hum of synth and his voice. He sings it close and cracked, the rasp catching as he switches between English, Pidgin and Twi. Produced by longtime collaborator Joker and released through EMPIRE, the single sits inside PUMA’s World Cup campaign for Ghana, whose Black Stars reach their fifth FIFA World Cup this summer across the United States, Canada and Mexico. The song returns to what Black Sherif has written about since Konongo, the mining town in Ghana’s Ashanti Region where he grew up: getting through long odds, holding on to belief, and carrying his people with him. He brought afrobeats, highlife and asakaa, the Ghanaian drill sound, together early on, and the new single works from the barest version of that: a guitar figure, a low synth bed and his voice. “Find A Way” follows “SWAGGA“, his return to hip-hop after he was named Artiste of the Year for the second time at the 2026 Telecel Ghana Music Awards, and it arrives as he moves toward his biggest New York headline show yet, at the Hammerstein Ballroom on 1 August. At 24, Black Sherif is already Ghana’s most-streamed artist: his debut The Villain I Never Was has passed three billion streams, and IRON BOY, released in 2025, has crossed one billion. items.body: Review by kev rowland — This album has been very slowly growing on me the more I have listened to it, but there is no way this stands up against the earlier classic releases, and the answer to that is pretty obvious, no guitarist and lead vocalist Roye Albrighton and the introduction (for this album only) of guitarist/vocalist Dave Nelson. The vocals were now split among the four musicians, there was a move to shorter songs and a more melodic rock/AOR approach, while Mick Brockett was no longer listed as a member of the band although he was still providing the special effects and lights he had always done, and was not in the band photo.This 3 CD reissue from Esoteric provides a lengthy essay from Mo Moore plus photos while on the musical front the first disc contains the same bonus tracks as the 2005 remaster, the second disc contains a live set from Hofstra University, Long Island October 1977 which was part of the 2014 remaster, while now we also get another live set on the third disc, this time from The Community Theater, Phoenix, November 1977. As always with anything coming from Cherry Red, the sound quality is excellent, and the album notes absolutely fascinating (I had no idea the model on the cover was a young Brooke Shields). But even the appearance of guests Larry Fast (Synergy, Peter Gabriel) and Robert Fripp (credited under the pseudonym Walt Nektroid) can prevent this from feeling quite bland and uninspiring. Given what was happening in the musical world at this time it is probably no surprise that this change of direction saw them lose the momentum they had been gaining from their earlier albums and the band dissolved the following year.I guess the question is whether this is worth seeking out? For a Nektar fan quite probably, especially for the live sets, but for the casual onlooker this is probably a pass. There is little in the way of true dynamics, and all the songs blur into each other. The passion had gone, and it shows. For me it is interesting to hear as I had not previously come across it, and as I said earlier, I enjoyed it much more after playing it a few times, but now the review is done I doubt I will ever listen to it again.
items._genre: psychedelic rock / space rock / progressive rock
items._cn_summary: 这张1977年的专辑是英国前卫摇滚乐队在转型期的作品，失去了原有的灵魂人物和吉他手，歌曲变得更短、更旋律化，朝向AOR方向靠拢。尽管有Larry Fast和Robert Fripp等客座乐手参与，但整体听起来平淡乏味，歌曲之间缺乏区分度，动态变化不足。Esoteric的3CD再版包含两张1977年的现场录音，音质出色，附有详尽的文字介绍和照片，但核心专辑本身的艺术水准明显不如乐队早期作品。对于新接触Nektar的听众来说，这张专辑并不具备足够的吸引力，乐评人自己也承认听完后很可能不会再播放。

items.body: Review by arcane-beautiful — I feel that this is the album where their newer sound fully took form. Taking their more focused songwriting based form of power prog metal with symphonic and oriental textures, I believe they took the place of the sexier side of the prog power metal world that Kamelot had with Roy Khan in the band. Overall the songwriting is pretty fantastic, with each song having great hooks, musicianship and masterclass vocals from Zaher Zorgati. While it has a more focused sound, there are moments where Malek Ben Arbia & Anis Jouini are able to show off some nice technical guitar and bass interplay. The production is pretty great too, even if on the CD version there's a massive drop in volume after the intro instrumental. The track I'd recommend is Believer.

The band
items.body: The Autumn Aurora “Plastic Altar” is the debut single from the Italian post-punk and darkwave band The Autumn Aurora, released on June 26, 2026 through Volcano Records. The “Plastic Altar” single arrives across digital platforms with an official music video. Plastic Altar by The Autumn Aurora The Autumn Aurora bring a post-punk and darkwave sound built on a rare lineup of two bass guitars, keyboards and drums, with a central passage that turns toward doom metal. The band cites Joy Division, The Cure and Siouxsie and the Banshees among its reference points. ‘Plastic Altar’: the debut single “Plastic Altar” streams on Spotify, Apple Music, Deezer, Bandcamp, SoundCloud and Tidal. The band recorded, mixed and mastered the track at GreenMountainAudio Studio with Danilo Silvestri, and frames the song around a “painful awakening” — the moment someone who has waited at an altar for a miracle realizes it will not come. The band released an official video for “Plastic Altar”: About The Autumn Aurora The Autumn Aurora is a Rome-based post-punk and darkwave band with a female-fronted lineup: Vera Perkins (vocals), Stefano Ferramola (bass), Francesca Buompane (bass), Chiara Bellucco (drums) and Fabrizio “Nemo” Mancini (keyboards). The two-bass setup, with no standard guitar, shapes the band’s low-end, atmospheric sound. “Plastic Altar,” released on June 26, 2026, is the band’s debut single and the first release from its forthcoming debut album “False Idols,” announced for September 11, 2026 on Volcano Records & Promotion, the Turin-based label.
items._cn_summary: 意大利罗马乐队 The Autumn Aurora 释出首支单曲《Plastic Altar》，由 Volcano Records 发行。乐队采用较为罕见的双贝斯编制，搭配键盘与鼓，女声主唱 Vera Perkins 居前，形成以低频和氛围为核心的暗潮基底，提及 Joy Division、The Cure 与 Siouxsie and the Banshees 作为参照。中段引入 doom metal 段落，使整体情绪由冷峻后朋克转向沉重缓慢的音墙。歌曲主题围绕对奇迹等待的破灭——在祭坛前终未等回应允的觉醒时刻。录制、混音与母带均在 GreenMountainAudio Studio 完成，与 Danilo Silvestri 合作。该单曲也是即将于九月发行的首张专辑《False Idols》的先导。作为首发新闻，缺乏对声音细节与编曲层次的深入评述，信息以厂牌发布为主。

items.body: Thalie Némésis, the French darkwave project of the musician Nathalie, released the album “Dé(s)figurations” on May 22, 2026 through Meridian Noir Records. The ten-track record is out on a limited CD-R and digital, and streams on Bandcamp. Thalie Némésis brings a darkwave that mixes coldwave and cold electronics with industrial textures and ritual, ethnic percussion. Dé(s)figurations by Thalie Némésis Inside Thalie Némésis ‘Dé(s)figurations’ “Dé(s)figurations” runs ten tracks: “A barbaric language,” “A demi-mots,” “Acedia (is my partner in crime),” “Cassandra (le baiser de la fin),” “No Surrender,” “Defixiones,” “Ruptures,” “Face to face (wild horses),” “Stormbreaker” and “Forget my name.” Thalie Némésis wrote the songs, with “Defixiones” co-written with Eva |3, and produced the album, which Peter Rainman mixed and mastered. The artwork is by Hervé Duhem, with photos by Martial Rossignol. The single “Stormbreaker” leads the album with an official video: About Thalie Némésis Thalie Némésis is the solo project of the French musician Nathalie, based in Aix-en-Provence. The project first appeared in 2013 and released early material in 2014, including work with Les Modules Étranges, before a long pause. Thalie Némésis returned with the 2025 EP “Catarsi Apotropaica,” which forms the first half of “Dé(s)figurations.” Nathalie co-founded Meridian Noir Records, a French label for dark alternative music, with Albin Wagener of The Memory of Snow, whose album “Inside” the label released in June 2026. “Dé(s)figurations,” out May 22, 2026, is the project’s latest release on Meridian Noir.
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑由法国音乐人Nathalie的独立项目Thalie Némésis发行，属于典型的暗潮/冷潮分支作品。整体制作将冷潮的极简电子骨架与工业质感纹理结合，并融入仪式化的民族打击乐元素，使听觉氛围带有原始部落的律动。十首曲目围绕宗教意象与古希腊神话展开，如'Acedia'、'Cassandra'、'Defixiones'等标题，暗示了概念上的黑暗叙事。混音与母带由Peter Rainman完成，视觉方面由Hervé Duhem操刀平面设计、Martial Rossignol负责摄影。这张唱片由厂牌Meridian Noir以限量CD-R与数字形式发行，属于小规模地下制作。从音乐信息来看，文章偏向新闻发布性质，缺乏对声音细节、编曲结构或情感表达的具体评论，听众难以从中获得关于实际聆听体验的有效参考。

items.body: Review by tszirmay — The Sheffield arranger, composer and multi-instrumentalist rises once again, landing straight to the top of the Symphonic prog pedestal with another outstanding release that merits the attention of all prog fans, his sixth venture that includes last year's 20th anniversary remake of his debut 2005 album "All in the Golden Afternoon". While all his records are of exceptional quality, as well as highly rated within the community, as he maintains a stylistic standard that is purely his own, this new opus might just conquer the prog Everest once and for all. So, when we talk about symphonic Prog , the two words are of maximal importance , as the balancing act required to blend the two together in harmonious deliverance is a challenging task. Arranging classical music, especially keyboard-based material is a bold enterprise, as the numerous prog legends of the glory years of the 70s stamped the rock element for eternity (we know who they are). Credibility, originality as well as respect of tradition are all required elements. Ian handles this arduous task by fully understanding how this brand of music needs to be listened to. The audience yearns for an immersive experience, with a time, a place and a story to plunge into with full engagement, in order to savor all the detailed components and how it will affect the pleasure nodes. From the three-part opening suite "How Dreams Do Creep (for Souls Asleep), to the sprawling "Leonardo" with its five acts , the casual listener is instantly drawn into abandoning any background music pretense, dropping all the multi-tasking maladies of our times , and just close the eyes, and let the imagination roam freely. That my friends is what music should be about: liberation. Ian wastes no time in establishing the foundational platform on which he will develop his craft on the opener, lessons learned from past innovators like early Genesis, including Ant Phillips (Slow Dance era) , as the delicate interface between the mellotron symphonics, the pastoral elements so dear to the British folk-rock tradition (The Strawbs, Gryphon, Magicfolk, Iona, etc?), and a brawny bass governance leaps forward throughout. Lather on some heady keyboards, both organ, piano, and synths, toss in some slicing guitar shavings and some serious syncopation on the percussive side, and you are immediately plunged into an alternate fantasy world of your own making. As if to further the point, "Late States , Eden's Gates" eliminates any possible argument that lethargic arrangements could rule the roost, quite to the contrary, the pace is throbbing, expansive, and at times, breathtakingly bold. That stodgy bass is such a devourer of emotions, egging on the remaining instrumental deliberations. A moment of reflection on the short "Enitharmon's Dream" wanders into dreamier territory yet still packs quite the wallop when challenged, very indicative of the album cover's intuitive message. The epic, nearly 13 minute "Cretan Angel" elects a mythological revisit of the Greek classics, your choice of Iliad or the Odyssey, a vocal and acoustic main frame on which to establish presence, a light passing through the veil of illusion, and a state of temporary silence. The progression is effortless, a gradual build-up of symphonic festivity, where details vie with overall impact for the attentive ear. The second half raises the temperature with stormier motifs, booming drums ushering in grandiose walls of synthesized orchestrations, and an expertly sculpted guitar solo that seek to rival the electronic keyboard arsenal, both putting up quite the fuss. The swirling finale is rightfully over the top. A duo of 5-minute pieces are next up, with "Fresco" surging into more delicate territory , a warm synth weaving between tick-tock drums, a massive synth-bass echoing throughout the musical cupola, craning necks desperate for focusing on the intricate details. The electric guitar solo overtly takes this straight into the celestial heavens, with a sprawling Gilmour-esque burst that screeches emphatically. Sublime. Another bucolic, flute-led orchestral romp on "Of Aether, Rose and Spangling Dew", the soaring harmonic chants a pure delicacy, church organ lagging close behind, cherubs looking down and smiling, establishing a comfortable numbness from which no one wishes to escape. Gloriously intense. The 11 and a quarter finale is the absolute highpoint, an exquisite exercise in cutting-edge, soundtrack-worthy cinematographic immersion. The stylishness of the piano, in tandem with its bass guitar counterpart, the eloquent choral voices, the euphoric cymbals crashing undeterred, as the melodic accrual marches onward and upward, is wholly phenomenal. The hushed lead vocals appear to express more than reverence, as the crescendo is ultimately attained and the whistling winds scatter the leaves of memories past. The evolution maintains nevertheless a continuity that keeps the focus on the overall canvas, adding a plethora of detail, power and insistence that was deliberately arranged to achieve a haunting apotheosis, perhaps even apocalyptic irrevocability. Symphonic Prog has a new classic to enjoy for ever more. Whatever your preferences are and how they may influence your choices, there is a time and a place for this style of escape within our over stimulated, at times helter-skelter (rarely has a Beatles title been more applicable to our current mayhem), and many would be negligent at their own peril of not checking out this gemlike flame! This release needs to be both heard and felt. 4.5 glittering emeralds
items._cn_summary: 这是一位英国全才音乐人的第六张专辑，以键盘为核心的交响前卫摇滚路线，承袭七十年代Genesis、Gryphon等乐队的传统手法。三段式开场组曲、五幕式长篇叙事以及近十三分钟的史诗曲目构成专辑骨架，融合mellotron交响音色、英国民谣田园元素、厚重的贝斯主导与键盘管风琴钢琴合成器层次，辅以切片式吉他和复杂节奏。评论强调沉浸式聆听体验，摒弃多任务习惯，让想象力自由驰骋。整体属于对经典流派传统的延续性致敬，技法扎实但风格框架明确，在创新性与跨类型融合方面未见突破，更偏向怀旧向的传统演绎，与用户偏好的实验、当代古典或暗潮电子方向存在较大距离。

items.body: Muse The Wow! Signal Muse's tenth album may be their most grandiose yet. Our man in high dudgeon, JR Moores goes track-by-track with Matt Bellamy and the boys The opening track on Muse’s tenth studio album contains the lyric “I’ve got absolutely nothing / Absolutely nothing new to say.” Only joking. That’s a line from ‘Empty Pledges’ by Yard Act. Imagine hearing that level of humility coming out the mouth of Matt Bellamy. It’d be as refreshing as Andrew Mountbatten releasing a cover version of Alice Cooper’s ‘Working Up A Sweat’. The actual first song on The Wow! Signal is called ‘The Dark Forest’ and naturally it’s all “abyss” this and “lonely stars” that. Therein lies the problem. This Teignmouth trio ran out of anything they had... The post Muse – The Wow! Signal appeared first on The Quietus.
items._genre: alternative rock / arena rock / progressive rock
items._cn_summary: 乐评指出Muse的第十张录音室专辑延续了宏大叙事的风格，开篇曲《The Dark Forest》充斥着'深渊'与'孤独星辰'等宇宙意象化的歌词。作者将乐队主唱Matt Bellam的自我表达与英国乐队Yard Act作品中罕见的谦逊态度形成对比，暗示Muse在这张作品中依然延续了夸张的修辞和庞大的空间感。评论以讽刺口吻切入，对乐队歌词内容的诚意与原创性提出质疑，认为这支来自Teignmouth的三人组在创作上已陷入自我重复的困境，整体姿态停留在戏剧化的摇滚表达层面，与前卫实验音乐的探索精神相距甚远。

items.body: Nachtmahr “Imperivm” is the new studio album from the Austrian industrial and EBM project Nachtmahr, released on June 26, 2026 through Trisol Music Group. The record is issued as a CD in an A5 digipack with booklet, and it follows the 2024 album “Verboten!“. “Imperivm” holds ten tracks and opens with “Wer Wind sät”. The full tracklist is “Wer Wind sät”, “Unterwerfung”, “Nie zurück”, “Das Böse”, “Stärker als ihr Hass”, “Infantil”, “Der Schlaf”, “Willenlos”, “Offenbarung” and “Neue Ufer”. This is the solo project of Thomas Rainer, who has run it since 2007 alongside his work in L’Âme Immortelle. About Nachtmahr Nachtmahr is an Austrian industrial and EBM project founded by Thomas Rainer in Vienna in 2007. Rainer started the project as an outlet for harder material while working as a resident DJ at Club Pi in Vienna, and ran it in parallel with L’Âme Immortelle, the darkwave duo he formed with Sonja Kraushofer in 1996. The first release, the EP “Kunst ist Krieg”, appeared in 2007 through Trisol Music Group. Studio albums followed with “Feuer Frei!” in 2008, “Alle Lust Will Ewigkeit” in 2009 and “Semper Fidelis” in 2010. The project became known for militaristic visuals and lyrics centered on power and control, presented across albums, EPs and live shows. The project kept that output running through the EP “Widerstand“ in 2018 and the picture-vinyl reissue of the mini-album “Mädchen in Uniform” in 2019. The project returned in 2020 with “Flamme“, issued the double album “Unbeugsam” in 2023, and released “Verboten!” through Trisol on November 1, 2024. With “Imperivm”, released on June 26, 2026, Nachtmahr extends that Trisol run into a new studio album, its first since “Verboten!”.
items._cn_summary: 这是一篇关于Nachtmahr新专辑《Imperivm》的纯新闻发布稿，介绍了专辑的基本信息：2026年6月26日通过Trisol Music Group发行，收录十首曲目，延续了自2024年《Verboten!》以来的创作脉络。Nachtmahr是奥地利音乐人Thomas Rainer自2007年以来的个人计划，同时他也是L'Âme Immortelle的成员。内容涵盖唱片格式（CD A5 digipack）、厂牌背景及项目的历史沿革，但未涉及任何音乐本体分析、声音设计探讨或艺术评价。文章完全缺乏对专辑音乐风格、编曲特点、制作水准或创新性的讨论，仅为信息性公告，不具备乐评深度。

items.body: Tiffadelic, a darkwave and post-punk artist from Detroit, has released the worldwide video premiere for her single “Blood Bath” on June 26, 2026. The track arrived earlier in 2026 through Darthpira Records and streams on Bandcamp. Tiffadelic brings a darkwave that mixes post-punk, minimal wave and synth, pairing haunting vocals with a spare approach to synthesizers and beat. Blood Bath by Tiffadelic The video for “Blood Bath” was shot and edited by the production team Dark Visionaries. The single was engineered, mixed and mastered by Detroit producer Steve Greene at Battle Chamber Studio. Here is the video for “Blood Bath”. About Tiffadelic Tiffadelic is a Detroit-based artist who mixes darkwave, post-punk, minimal wave and synth, and describes herself as a “Black Goth” artist. She released her debut album, “Retrosynthesis Vol. I,” in September 2025 through Darthpira Records, a nine-track record issued on limited-edition gold cassette and produced with Steve Greene. Earlier singles include “I Tried” and “Nazareth (B.O.P).” The “Blood Bath” single followed in early 2026, with its video premiere on June 26, 2026. Verified background on the artist beyond her releases is limited at the time of writing.

items.body: Review by kev rowland — Unless you have been under a rock somewhere you will know that Rush are not the only Canadians making an unexpected comeback in 2026, as the original line-up of Mike Levine (bass, keyboards, synthesizer, piano, backing vocals), Gil Moore (drums, percussion, lead and backing vocals and Rik Emmett (guitar, lead and backing vocals, synthesizer, keyboards, bass) are also hitting the road. Of course there will always be a record label tie-in, and as there is no new product to release, we instead have another compilation of their greatest hits (many of which are single edits). I have all the albums featuring the original guys, having first discovered them when they released the single "Hold On" which soon led me to buying their third album, 1979's 'Just A Game'. Their technical melodic hard rock was a style I really enjoyed, a long way from the NWOBHM scene I was experiencing as a teenager in the UK, and playing this album now is like visiting old friends.Every song contained on this 10-track set was a hit single in Canada or America, but I was somewhat surprised to see that "I Live For The Weekend" was missing as that has always been one of my favourites (I have it as a 12" single) but then realised that for some weird reason it was only a hit in the UK. But given it was the only song of theirs to ever chart there it would have been nice to see it, but I guess Americans/Canadians may not see it that way. This is a great introduction to one of Canada's greatest ever hard rock exports, and while their return may been overshadowed somewhat, there is no doubt they are worthy inductees to the Canadian Music Industry Hall of Fame, the Canadian Music Hall of Fame, and Canada's Walk of Fame, even if there has been no new studio album since 1992. "Lay It On The Line", "Hold On", "Magic Power", "I Can Survive" are all here, ans in many ways this is a solid release.

items._cn_summary: 这是一篇关于1986年《新世纪风景系列》合辑的简短介绍，由Michael Tucker撰写。专辑收录了John Themis、Tom Newman、Tim Cross和Dashiell Rae四位音乐家的作品，探讨了新世纪音乐与爵士之间曾经被混淆的历史关联。文章主要是对四十年前新世纪音乐兴起的回顾，内容信息量极为有限，未能深入分析各曲目的音乐特征、编曲手法或演奏细节。从风格定位来看，新世纪音乐属于轻量级环境音乐范畴，与用户偏好的实验前卫、自由即兴、电子先锋及暗潮工业等方向相距甚远，且文章本身缺乏实质性乐评内容，仅为新闻性质的转载摘要，无法提供足够的音乐判断依据。

items.body: The band will put out expanded editions of the albums Vanishing Point, XTRMNTR and Evil Heat over the remainder of the year Screenshot Primal Scream are releasing expanded editions of their albums Vanishing Point (1997), XTRMNTR (2000) and Evil Heat (2002). Making up The Bunker Trilogy, the series of releases will take in newly remastered editions of all three records, as well as unheard material, B-sides and new liner notes. Each album will be reissued digitally, as well as on vinyl and CD. The series kicks off with Vanishing Point's reissue on 7 August, while XTRMNTR will follow on 4 September. The band will round off the run of releases with Evil Heat on 30 October. Commenting on the reissues, Primal Scream frontman Bobby Gillespie said:... items.body: 「音楽」に深いこだわりを持つ飲食店を紹介するこのコーナー。今回は、西荻窪（東京都杉並区）にあるリスニングカフェ＆バー『JUDGMENT! RECORDS lounge（ジャッジメントレコード ラウンジ）』を訪問。「和ジャズ」の火付け役であり、ジャズ好きには広く知られる人物のお店ながら、デートでも使える気軽さが魅力でした。 西荻窪駅から徒歩1分のリスニングカフェ＆バー JR中央・総武線 西荻窪駅北口から徒歩約1分、角にカラオケ館のある小道を入った雑居ビル3Fにある『JUDGMENT! RECORDS lounge（ジャッジメントレコード ラウンジ）』。西荻窪（東京都杉並区）は、吉祥寺ほど商業化されておらず、高円寺ほどサブカル色が強すぎずない絶妙なエリアといえる。また、以前紹介したROLLINGAを始め、話題のミュージックバーが立て続けにオープンしている注目スポットでもある。 そんな場所で2026年4月に誕生したのが、ジャズを中心とする中古レコード店『JUDGMENT! RECORDS』が手がけるリスニングカフェ＆バーだ。ちなみに、店主の塙 耕記さんはかつてディスクユニオンのジャズ統括責任者であり、「和ジャズ」の火付け役としても知られている。 「東京には老舗のジャズ喫茶や有名なジャズバーがたくさんあるので、そこに対抗するような気持ちはないんです。リスニング カフェ＆バーとライトな表現をしているように、20～30代の若い人たち、音楽やレコードに興味がない人たちに、どんどん来てもらいたい。そのうえで、“なんか音がいいね” “いい曲だね” “ジャズっていいね” ”レコードも買えるんだ” と、ちょっと裾野を広げたいなという意識でやっています」。そう語る塙さん。 店内はテーブル＆ソファが16席、カウンター5席と広々としている。ミッドセンチュリーの家具を配した店内は洗練されており、平日はバーとして土曜はカフェ＆バーとして誰でも気軽に利用することができる。 さりげなく置かれるミッドセンチュリーの家具たち 「ミッドセンチュリーの家具は20代の頃から集めていて、イームズやベルトイア、柳宗理などのチェアを並べています。ソファ席はジャパニーズコーナーとして、カリモクで揃えました」 他にも、スペースエイジデザインなオーディオシステム「Weltron 2007」も置かれているが、レトロフューチャーな店内というわけではない。 「床を張り替えたり、一部の壁を塗り直したりなどしていますが、居抜きの内装を生かしながら家具をセレクトしていきました」 70年代〜現代のレコードに合わせたサウンドシステム 残置物の中には、アルテックのヴァレンシアがあったというから驚きだ。塙さんは「そんなに好きなスピーカーじゃないですけど」と笑いながら話すが、せっかくだからとヴァレンシアに合うオーディオをセレクトしていった。 ターンテーブルはモーファイ・エレクトロニクス、アンプはマッキントッシュのMA6100、CDプレーヤーはケンブリッジオーディオ。また、家電製品からのノイズ干渉を防ぐため、単独回路の電源を新設したという。 「東中野のお店（JUDGMENT! RECORDS）は、オリジナル盤のレコードがよく鳴るようにヴィンテージの機材で統一しているんです。でも、このお店でかけるのは再発盤や国内盤が多くなるので、70年代から現代のプレスのレコードに合わせたサウンドシステムにしています」 それぞれの楽器が際立つクリアさがありながら、全体として大迫力のサウンド。カウンターで聴けば、スマホを忘れてつい音楽に没頭してしまうだろう。一方、テーブル席なら会話を楽しみながら、音楽の魅力に気づくことができる。 「基本的にはジャズのアルバムを片面ずつ、昼間のカフェ営業だったらボサノバやブラジル系をかけたりもします。そういう意味では、お客さんの雰囲気と時間帯を気にしながら選盤しています」 店内には、JUDGMENT! RECORDSから流動的にセレクトされるタイトル、これまで塙さんが関わったブルーノートなどの名盤系や、現在監修中の和ジャズを代表するレーベルであるスリー・ブラインド・マイス（TBM）など、常時1000枚ほど用意されているという。 「中古レコード店もやっているので、一般的なジャズ喫茶のように、これを揃えなくてはという感覚はまったくないんです。なので、お店に置いているレコードも流動的。そのうえで、この人はモダンジャズが好きそうだなとか、この人は詳しいからマイナーなものをかけてみようとか、そういう感じでやっていますね」 『JUDGMENT! RECORDS lounge』は、音楽や音響だけでなく、お酒や珈琲、紅茶が抜群に美味しいという魅力もある。 「しっかりとしたものを提供したいので、まずはバーの姿勢や取り組み方について、親交のあるバーの方に全スタッフ揃えて研修してもらいました。日々学びながら、基本に忠実にやっています。珈琲に関しても週イチで来てもらっているバリスタがいて、彼女の指導のもと淹れています。豆に関してもバリスタの自家焙煎で『BLOOM as you are.』というブランド名で販売もしてます。紅茶も丁寧にポットで提供していて好評です」 ジャズ喫茶を営む両親のもとで生まれ育った 塙さんは、水戸市のジャズ喫茶『The Sound & The Fury』を営む両親のもとで生まれ育った。幼少期から家に大量のレコードがあり、クルマで出かければ大音量でジャズがかかっていたという。 「アコースティックなジャズ・スタンダードはまだしも、マイルス・デイビスの『ビッチェズ・ブリュー』など、エレクトリック期のマイルスを大音量で聴かされるのは苦痛でしたよ（笑）」 小学生の頃は周囲と同じように歌謡曲を聴いていたが、テレビの前にラジカセを置いて音楽番組を録音するなど、人よりも少しだけ音楽好きだったという。その後、中学でオールディーズが好きになり、そこからリトル・リチャードなど黒人音楽も聴くようになる。 「そうすると、ホーンの音色が入ってきたりするじゃないですか。そこから楽器に興味を持ち始めて、高校くらいから少しずつジャズも聴くようになったんです」 その後、進学のために20歳で上京。そこからレコード屋巡りが加熱する。一度は不動産会社に就職するものの、すぐに辞めてディスクユニオンに転職。運よくジャズ担当になり、これまで知らなかった現代のジャズプレイヤーなどを必死に勉強しながらメキメキと頭角を現していった。 「90年代の話ですが、いろいろとジャズを聴くうちに“日本人の古いジャズが面白いぞ”と思うようになって。ちょこちょこ買って集めていたんですけど、当時は馬鹿にされるんですよ。でも、良いものは良いので、復刻を中心とした自社レーベルが発足したタイミングでCD化していったんです」 その後、『ジャズ批評』が日本のジャズを特集。そこで初めて「和ジャズ」という言葉が生まれ、一気に広がっていったという。その流れを汲み、尾川雄介氏と共に書籍『和ジャズ・ディスク・ガイド Japanese Jazz 1950s-1980s』（2009年）を出版。今や、古き良き「和ジャズ」は世界にまで広がることになった。そして、塙さんは2022年に独立をする。 他にもたくさんの功績があるのだが、塙さんの経歴を知ると「ジャズマニアが集まるお店」と思われてしまうかもしれない。しかし、そんなことはまったくないので安心してほしい。冒頭にあった開店の経緯のように、まずはただのオシャレなカフェ、いい感じのバーを目指して出向くのが正解だ。 「お客さんと会話するのも好きですし、お酒のつくり方を日々勉強しながら“うわっ、美味しくできた！”とかやっているので、毎日すごく楽しいですよ」 いい音で美味しいお酒や珈琲を楽しみたい、そんな気分のときはふらり立ち寄ってみてはいかがだろう。 取材・文／富山英三郎 撮影／高瀬竜弥 ・店舗名 JUDGMENT! items.body:
BINI have officially kicked off their second world tour in spectacular fashion, opening the Signals World Tour with two sold-out nights at the Mall of Asia Arena on 20 and 21 June.

The nation's girl group delivered a high-energy set that celebrated both a new era and the songs that helped define their rise. Fans were among the first to experience live performances of new tracks 'Step Back' and 'Sugar Rush', while longtime BLOOMs sang along to favourites including 'I Feel Good', 'Lagi', 'Na Na Na', and 'Unang Kilig'.

The Manila concerts quickly became one of the country's biggest online talking points, topping Philippine trends on X across both show dates as fans shared clips, reactions, and highlights from the production.

Beyond the group's own catalogue, BINI surprised the crowd with special stages that showcased their versatility. The octet performed Sarah Geronimo's 'Duyan' and Donnalyn Bartolome's 'Kakaibabe', while also bringing back the Coachella set that won over audiences earlier this year. Another standout moment came with the live performance of 'A Parallel World', which is set to appear on the official soundtrack of the upcoming animated film Forgotten Island.

With Manila in the books, the Signals World Tour heads to Cebu on 11 July for another sold-out show. The concert will also mark the first live event to be staged at the new SM Seaside Cebu Arena.

The momentum continues overseas in August, when BINI embarks on an 11-city North American run beginning in Honolulu before making stops across the United States and Canada, bringing Filipino pop to audiences across the continent.

Fresh off a triumphant hometown launch, Signals is already shaping up to be BINI's biggest tour yet, with sold-out crowds and an ambitious international schedule signalling the group's continued rise on the global stage.

items.excerpt: 会期：2026/03/27～2026/08/09 会場：21_21 DESIGN SIGHTギャラリー1&2［東京都］ 公式サイト：https://www.2121designsight.jp/program/soup/ 「スープを入り口に、衣食住の根源を見つめる」という着眼点はとてもユニークだと思った。衣と住が身体の外側の環境で、食が内側の環境であり、いずれも「身体を包む行為」と捉える発想はこれまで考えもしなかったけれど、言われてみればそのとおりである。さらにその視点は母体へと移り、「生まれる前の私たちは、母体という“住”、胞衣（えな／胎膜・胎盤など）という“衣”、そして羊水という“食”に」包まれていたというメッセージを掲げる。展覧会ディレクターを務めた遠山夏未は、イッセイ ミヤケで衣服のデザインをする傍ら、そうした考えに至り、著書『ポタージュ──野菜たっぷり家族のスープ』（池田書店、2014）を上梓するなど、スープに着目した活動を行なっている人物だ。食から人間や社会を取り巻く環境を考える試みはよくあるが、食という漠然とした概念より、スープという最小限のコンテンツをてこにする方が断然
items.body: 会期：2026/03/27～2026/08/09 会場：21_21 DESIGN SIGHTギャラリー1&2［東京都］ 公式サイト：https://www.2121designsight.jp/program/soup/ 「スープを入り口に、衣食住の根源を見つめる」という着眼点はとてもユニークだと思った。衣と住が身体の外側の環境で、食が内側の環境であり、いずれも「身体を包む行為」と捉える発想はこれまで考えもしなかったけれど、言われてみればそのとおりである。さらにその視点は母体へと移り、「生まれる前の私たちは、母体という“住”、胞衣（えな／胎膜・胎盤など）という“衣”、そして羊水という“食”に」包まれていたというメッセージを掲げる。展覧会ディレクターを務めた遠山夏未は、イッセイ ミヤケで衣服のデザインをする傍ら、そうした考えに至り、著書『ポタージュ──野菜たっぷり家族のスープ』（池田書店、2014）を上梓するなど、スープに着目した活動を行なっている人物だ。食から人間や社会を取り巻く環境を考える試みはよくあるが、食という漠然とした概念より、スープという最小限のコンテンツをてこにする方が断然伝わりやすい。そしてスープといえば、誰もが湯気の立った温かなイメージを抱きやすいという点で、会場全体が何ともいえない幸福感に満ちあふれていたのである。 展示風景 21_21 DESIGN SIGHTギャラリー2 ISSEY MIYAKE＋林響太朗＋長尾智子《色をまとい、色を味わう ―身体を染める色と味―》（部分）［撮影：木奥恵三］ ギャラリー1では「包まれる」と題され、遠山夏未＋岡篤郎＋NOTA&design（加藤駿介、加藤佳世子）によるインスタレーション《はじまりのスープ》が展示されていた。本展に通底するテーマがまさに体現されており、それは息を呑むほどの迫力だ。ギャラリー2では「集まる」と題された空間に、和紙に土を混ぜ込んだ土紙による屋根が天井から吊るされ、映像による“火”も灯されて、そこに原初的な住まいの姿を見ることができた。大きな布の敷かれた“座敷”に靴を脱いで上がると、卓上ではさまざまなクリエイターが持ち寄った「旅とスープ」の思い出に触れることができる。 展示風景 21_21 DESIGN SIGHTギャラリー1 遠山夏未＋岡篤郎＋NOTA&design（加藤駿介、加藤佳世子）《はじまりのスープ》［撮影：木奥恵三］ 展示風景 21_21 DESIGN SIGHTギャラリー2［撮影：木奥恵三］ 展示風景 21_21 DESIGN SIGHTギャラリー2 佐藤政人《世界のスープ図鑑》［撮影：木奥恵三］ しかし、なんだろう。鑑賞後、何か心に引っ掛かったのは、これらの牧歌的な展示作品と現実との間にあまりに隔たりがあるからに違いない。実際には食を取り巻く社会環境は非常に複雑を極めている。世界のあちこちで農薬や化学肥料などによる土壌汚染や生態系破壊は進んでいるし、食のグローバル化の促進によってフードマイレージも高まっている。食への根源的な意識を向けさせるという点では、本展は成功しているのかもしれない。さらに、ここから一歩進んだ行動を起こせるか否かが、我々に仕向けられた試練ともいえる。 鑑賞日：2026/05/28（木）

items.body: I can’t hear that he’s calling my name The sound is drowned out in the rain Shots ring out in the night Some moments refuse to remain in the past. They return in fragments: a face suspended in memory, a sound drowned out by rain, a story replayed frame by frame until the mind begins mistaking its repetition for control. Grief carries its own damaged signal, breaking apart and reassembling itself in flashes. The more one tries to recover the moment that cannot be undone, the more distorted it becomes. Washington, D.C. dark synthpop duo 2DCAT step into that unresolved space with the video for “Frames (Blue Rose Edit).” The track reworks “Frames,” a fan favourite the band loved but, by Johan Hauck’s own assessment, could never quite survive in a live set. The Blue Rose Remix of the track answers that problem by turning restraint into force. “Frames was a song our fans loved and we could never play live,” says Hauck. “The Blue Rose remix is me solving that problem with a sledgehammer. Literally.” That is not a metaphor. The primary snare line driving the remix was recorded at a county landfill, where Hauck took his self-built, LMD-649-inspired sampler and captured the sound of metal components being smashed and machinery being thrown into other machinery. Recorded through a 12-bit, 50 kHz capture chain, those impacts became the track’s percussive spine: not programmed violence, but found wreckage converted into rhythm. The result carries the same grief-stricken lyrics as the original—helplessness, loss, and the sickening recognition of a moment that cannot be reversed—but the body around them has changed. The remix is harder, faster, and more physically insistent, pushing the song toward the dance floor without sanding away its sorrow. Its pulse feels forged rather than sequenced, closer in spirit to Einstürzende Neubauten treating industrial debris as an instrument than to a track built entirely inside a digital workstation. Hauck’s machinery is central to the sound. Every synthesizer on “Frames” was built from his own designs, using 16nm Xilinx FPGAs as their backbone. His sampler, constructed from scratch, takes inspiration from the LMD-649, the Toshiba-EMI digital sampler developed by engineer Kenji Murata in the 1970s. Hauck reconstructed his own version from limited circuit specifications and historically plausible components, creating a machine that now follows 2DCAT onto the stage. Around that hardware-driven violence, HAEZL remains the emotional centre of the song. An acclaimed opera singer, she brings precision and weight without overstatement: the diction is sharp, the range controlled, and the delivery heavy with the kind of grief that does not need to announce itself theatrically to be devastating. In the repeated admission “I couldn’t save you,” the song finds its wound and refuses to close it. The Blue Rose designation points directly toward David Lynch. In Lynch’s world, a blue rose marks the kind of case that cannot be explained by ordinary means, something resistant to resolution. That logic fits “Frames”: a song about loss that does not settle into understanding, but instead remains suspended in the in-between, where memory becomes evidence and evidence becomes haunted. The accompanying video extends that idea through stark black-and-white imagery and deliberate analog damage. It opens with blown-out machinery, glare, and a flickering title card before giving way to HAEZL’s face, partially obscured by horizontal smears, scratches, and ghosted signal breaks. Her image appears close enough to touch, then slips behind interference. Performance footage places the duo inside a severe, high-contrast space framed by radiant light bars and deep pools of shadow. Hauck stands at the machinery while HAEZL moves through the foreground like a figure caught between transmission and apparition. The frame repeatedly tears, blooms, and bends; light flares swallow the image; faces double and dissolve; and the screen itself seems to become unstable under the pressure of the song. Those distortions are not decorative glitches. The video draws on the signal-processing and video-art legacy of Steina and Woody Vasulka, whose work treated electronic degradation as a compositional material rather than a flaw to be corrected. Feedback ghosts, tear bends, and other analog artifacts become part of the visual language here, mirroring the way the remix turns landfill percussion and damaged signal into melody, texture, and momentum. At times, the video feels like a broadcast from a machine that has learned to mourn. The images do not simply illustrate the song’s grief; they behave like grief itself—looping, fragmenting, overexposing, and returning to the same impossible frame. By the end, “Frames (Blue Rose Edit)” has transformed loss into motion without pretending that motion is the same as escape. Watch the video for “Frames (Blue Rose Edit)” below: Based in Washington, D.C., 2DCAT are a dark synthpop and darkwave duo inspired by the late ’70s and early ’80s European synth music scene. Their live sets have brought them to sold-out club nights and festival stages across the United States and Europe, drawing from darkwave, synthpop, and gothic audiences. “Frames (Blue Rose Edit)” is out now. Listen to the song below, and order it here. items.body: Black stars are shining from the deep I hide from But this road may carry me home Some songs begin with a map in their pocket and spend their running time trying to decide whether to follow it. Giant Crow’s beautiful ballad Home, the second single from the upcoming studio album Neodemon, carries that restless feeling from its first breath. Following their 2024 debut album In the Cut and the folk-influenced single Wildfire from the forthcoming album, the band shifts focus to the expansive realm of post-rock on Home. Here, emotion builds gradually and patiently before finally gaining the courage to take flight. Home has the dusky grandeur of Richard Hawley, the aching romantic voltage of Roy Orbison, and the lonely highway glow of Chris Isaak, all filtered through a band more interested in atmosphere than theatrics. The vocal performance carries a deep, handsome ache, with enough restraint to let the words breathe and enough drama to make each phrase feel carved from private experience. Around it, the guitars widen by degrees, the rhythm section holds its nerve, and the arrangement echoes how grief often moves in circles before it ever moves forward. Lyrically, Home follows a figure walking through darkness in search of purpose, surrender, and some possible return to belonging. Black stars, firelit fields, trees, family, and buried violence pass through the song like images seen from a moving car at dawn. There is memory here, but also inheritance; the sense that pain can travel through bloodlines, through silence, through the roads people take when staying put becomes impossible. The refrain’s hope feels hard-earned, less like comfort than a wager placed against despair. The video deepens that idea with a rocket launch, turning departure into a strange act of healing. Earth, the most precious home we have, falls away beneath fire and vapour, while the song stretches into its expansive shoegaze outro. The image is bittersweet without being heavy-handed: to move past grief, the clip suggests, one may have to leave the known world behind for a while. As the rocket speeds away from the planet and into the great unknown, Home finds its most ecstatic contradiction, making exile feel briefly weightless. Watch the video for Home below: By the end, Giant Crow have made a song about return that keeps looking outward. “Home” understands that the road back may pass through fire, silence, family memory, and even the heavens before it bends toward peace. It is grand without losing tenderness, wounded without begging for sympathy, and spacious enough to let the listener bring their own ghosts along for the ride.
